endorsements.quote: Prospective studies — such as clusterrandomized or stepped-wedge trials — are needed to assess impacts on response times, hospitalization rates, preventive care uptake, and clinician burnout, including from“alert fatigue”.

unlisted_practices: Continuously monitor deployed AI through periodic audits and user feedback to reduce risks of inaccuracy, bias, harm, or lack of adaptability.
Routinely update predictive models so they remain adaptive as patient demographics and social determinants evolve.
Provide transparent and interactive AI systems that give clear rationales for their suggestions to counter automation bias.
Design AI outreach to be personalized, culturally appropriate, and barrier-conscious rather than simply automating existing outreach approaches.
Design population health AI to prioritize patients by medical need rather than by which patients initiate contact or schedule visits.
Integrate longitudinal patient data from EHRs, claims, health information exchanges, and social service databases into population-level AI monitoring.

screen.reason: Commentary discussing considerations, strategies, and best practices for deploying and optimizing AI in population health management within primary care.
